provenance: Assistant-authored development search/comparison checks frozen after source scouting and before records or vocabulary changes. Expected useful cases are provisional starting points, not exhaustive relevance grades or independent validation.
policy: Use one fixed extended input vocabulary for old and expanded collections, with identical eligibility rules. Record original M006/old-collection output separately to distinguish vocabulary effects. Do not retune ranking or update expectations after seeing outputs.

comparison_records.purpose: Read falling versus rising dairy costs, annual consolidated scope, gross-margin definitions, benchmark versus company cost, source locators and unknowns. No arithmetic comparison or causal inference.

records.business_scope: Consolidated continuing U.S. dairy and dairy-case products business; excludes disposed WhiteWave and Morningstar operations

metric.name: Gross margin
metric.basis: Reported US accounting calculation: gross profit divided by net sales. Some finished-product delivery/shipping costs are in selling and distribution expenses, rather than cost of sales.
metric.scope: Consolidated continuing operations, U.S. dairy business
metric.comparison: Calendar 2015 versus 2014: 17.6%; WhiteWave and Morningstar shown as discontinued operations

evidence.locator: Item 7 MD&A, Year Ended December 31, 2015 Compared to 2014, Cost of Sales and Gross Profit, printed p. 24; Note 1 Shipping and Handling Fees, printed p. F-8; MD&A Overview p. 21

figures.name: Class I raw-milk price benchmark
figures.basis: Average monthly Class I mover benchmark, quoted per hundredweight (100 pounds). NOT the price Dean actually paid: location differences, producer premiums and procurement costs also matter.
figures.scope: U.S. federal raw-milk benchmark reported by Dean; not company purchase-price scope
figures.comparison: 2015 average versus 2014 average of US$23.29 per 100 lb; reported change −29.8%

evidence.locator: MD&A raw-milk price table and footnotes, printed p. 24

records.comparison_limit: Falling dairy costs, rather than inflation. Gross margin excludes some delivery costs that other companies include in cost of sales.
unknowns: Actual average milk purchase price, including location premiums and procurement costs.
The isolated effects of prices, cost programmes and lower input costs.
When the cost decline began/ended and later outcomes.

metric.name: Gross margin
metric.basis: Reported consolidated gross margin; sales less cost of sales, divided by sales
metric.comparison: FY2006 ended 28 May 2006: 35.6%; FY2007 ended 27 May 2007

evidence.locator: Item 6, Selected Financial Data, Operating Ratios, gross margin row, FY2007/FY2006 (printed p. 12)

figures.name: Higher ingredient and energy costs
figures.basis: Company-reported year-on-year cost increase; ingredients primarily grains and dairy, plus energy. This is not the total change in cost of sales.

evidence.locator: Item 7, MD&A, Fiscal 2007 Consolidated Results, printed p. 14, cost-of-sales paragraph and following paragraph

records.comparison_limit: A full financial year across a packaged-food company; gross margin rose despite higher ingredient and energy costs.
unknowns: How much of the cost increase came from each ingredient or energy.
The separate effect and timing of each action.
When the pressure began and ended, and what happened later.

comparison_records.purpose: Compare coffee segment profit, beef segment operating loss and bottler gross margin without conflating accounting measures, quarterly/annual periods or independent company claims.

records.business_scope: U.S. Retail Coffee Market segment: domestic retail Folgers, Dunkin’ Donuts and Millstone coffee

metric.name: Segment profit margin
metric.basis: Revenue less direct and allocable operating expenses, divided by segment sales; includes segment intangible-asset amortization/impairment under the revised 2011 calculation. Not company-wide gross margin. Interest, corporate administration, share-based compensation, merger/integration and restructuring costs are outside the segment-profit total in the Note E reconciliation.
metric.comparison: FY2011 ended 30 April versus FY2010 ended 30 April: 28.5%; FY2010 conformed to the 2011 calculation

evidence.locator: MD&A pp. 24–25; Note E Reportable Segments pp. 48–49

figures.name: Change in segment profit
figures.basis: Reported year-on-year profit growth, rounded; an increase in profit dollars can coexist with a lower profit margin

evidence.locator: MD&A, U.S. Retail Coffee Market, printed p. 25; segment comparison table p. 24

records.comparison_limit: A U.S. retail-coffee division, using segment profit rather than company-wide gross margin. The prior-year segment calculation was restated.
unknowns: The separate contribution of pricing, marketing and product changes to profit.
Coffee species, purchase timing and hedge effects within this segment.
True pressure boundaries and later results.
This source was filed 28 June 2011; it is not a claim that none of its facts were public earlier.

records.business_scope: Beef reportable segment, not Tyson’s chicken/pork/prepared-food segments

metric.name: Reported operating income (loss)
metric.basis: Reported operating income/loss under standard US accounting rules; includes inventory valuation, legal, plant-closure and restructuring effects
metric.comparison: Fiscal Q1 2024 (1 October–30 December 2023) versus fiscal Q1 2023 ended 31 December 2022: US$166 million profit

evidence.locator: Item 2 MD&A, Beef Segment Results, printed p. 29

figures.name: Estimated increase in cattle costs
figures.basis: Approximate company cost-bridge attribution, not total consolidated cost growth or an isolated estimate of its profit effect

evidence.locator: MD&A Cost of Sales bridge, printed p. 27

figures.name: Inventory write-down affecting operating income
figures.basis: Inventory reduced to the lower of cost or expected realizable value; this accounting charge is separate from the cattle purchase-cost increase
figures.comparison: Charge in fiscal Q1 2024; not presented as a year-on-year price change

evidence.locator: Item 2 MD&A, Beef Segment Results, printed p. 29

records.comparison_limit: A meat-processing division with a quarterly operating loss. Inventory valuation, legal and closure charges also affect the result; it is not a pure cattle-cost measure.
unknowns: How much of the operating loss is attributable to cattle costs alone.
Savings specifically achieved by the two plant closures.
True pressure boundaries, later results and the full purchase-price/hedge timing profile.

records.business_scope: U.S. consolidated bottling/distribution business, predominantly nonalcoholic beverages; not The Coca-Cola Company’s global concentrate business

metric.name: Gross margin
metric.basis: Reported gross profit divided by net sales under standard US accounting rules; includes specified plant-to-distribution shipping/fuel costs in cost of sales, while other delivery costs are outside it
metric.scope: Consolidated U.S. bottler and other operations
metric.comparison: Calendar 2022 versus 2021: 35.1%; reported increase 160 basis points

evidence.locator: Item 7 MD&A, Executive Summary, printed p. 22; Cost of Sales definition p. 24

figures.name: Estimated increase in input costs
figures.basis: Approximate company estimate including aluminum, PET resin and transportation. Not an aluminum-only amount and not the total cost-of-sales change; mix also affected costs.
figures.scope: Consolidated bottling business and other operations

evidence.locator: Item 7 MD&A Cost of Sales, printed p. 24

records.comparison_limit: A U.S. bottler rather than a global brand/concentrate company. Gross margin rose despite higher inputs; the company also discussed pricing, product mix and some later commodity moderation.
unknowns: The separate amounts for aluminum, bottle resin and transport within the cost estimate.
How much each pricing or operating action changed margin.
The true pressure start/end and later outcomes.
